name: Sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia (double detonation)
blurb: A 1 M☉ carbon-oxygen white dwarf under a thin helium shell, set alight at the base of the shell at its pole. The helium detonation wraps around the star and drives a shock into the core, which converges off center and can ignite carbon: the double-detonation model of Type Ia supernovae. Burned by the trained aprox13 network.

featured.label: Mass (M☉)
featured.tip: Mass of the white dwarf, core and shell, in solar masses. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Helium shell (M☉)
featured.tip: Mass of the helium shell, in solar masses: the outermost mass of the star. Thin shells (0.01-0.05) are what make normal Type Ia supernovae; too thin and the helium does not detonate at this resolution. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Ignition temperature (10⁹ K)
featured.tip: Temperature of the hot spot that sets the helium alight, in 1e9 K. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Hot spot radius (km)
featured.tip: Radius of the hot spot, in km, centered one radius above the base of the shell on the +z axis. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Burn inside shocks
featured.tip: Let cells the shock detector flags burn (1) or not (0). Off, as in most supernova codes: a captured shock is a few cells of numerical smearing. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Burning limiter f
featured.tip: No cell takes in burning energy faster than f times its internal energy per sound crossing of the cell (Kushnir et al. 2013); 0 switches it off (the default). Changing it starts the run again
